extraction_metadata.notes: Gate-based quantum algorithm: quantum short-step interior-point method (QIPM) for second-order cone programs (SOCP) reducing constrained portfolio optimization. Provable complexity O~(n * sqrt(r) * zeta * kappa / delta^2 * log(1/eps)). Experiments are classical simulations of the quantum-noise model (Gaussian noise calibrated to tomography precision) on S&P 500 sub-samples from cvxportfolio; they estimate empirical scaling of problem-dependent parameters (kappa, delta, zeta) and overall complexity.

summary: First quantum algorithm for CONSTRAINED portfolio optimization (positivity + budget constraints). Reduces the problem to an SOCP and applies a quantum short-step interior-point method using block encodings, quantum linear-system solvers and quantum tomography. Theoretical runtime O~(n * sqrt(r) * kappa * zeta / delta^2 * log(1/eps)) versus classical O~(sqrt(r) * n^omega * log(1/eps)) with practical omega~3. Experiments on S&P-500 sub-samples from cvxportfolio (50 companies, 100 days, 9-year dataset 2007-2016) simulate the quantum noise with Gaussian tomography-precision noise. Empirical findings: kappa shows no growth with problem size, zeta < 5 for all instances, 1/delta^2 grows roughly linearly with n (power-law exponent 1.050, 95% CI [0.965, 1.136]), overall observed complexity scales as O(n^2.387) with 95% CI [2.184, 2.589] -- giving an almost O(n) speedup over the practical classical O(n^3.5).

experiments.description: Simulation of the quantum short-step SOCP IPM on S&P-500 sub-samples from cvxportfolio: 50 companies x 100 days baseline, plus random subsets of 100 companies over random windows t in [10, 500] days, precision eps=0.1. Quantum noise modelled as Gaussian with magnitude equal to tomography precision. Measured: duality gap decay, Newton-matrix condition number kappa, zeta, 1/delta^2, and overall observed runtime scaling.

algorithm.variant: Quantum short-step interior-point method for Second-Order Cone Programs (QIPM-SOCP) [Kerenidis-Prakash-Szilagyi 2019, building on Kerenidis-Prakash SDP IPM]
algorithm.ansatz: SOCP reduction: min (1;0_{n+m})^T (t;x) s.t. Mx = tilde_t, mu^T x = R, Ax = b, x>=0, t in Lorentz cone L^m. Block-encoded Newton system solved via QRAM-based linear algebra (Chakraborty-Gilyen-Jeffery; Gilyen-Su-Low-Wiebe) with tomography (Kerenidis-Prakash).
algorithm.optimizer: Classical outer IPM loop; inner step = quantum linear-system solve + quantum state tomography + norm estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio covariance Sigma=M M^T with columns (1/sqrt(T-1))(R(t)-mu) stored in QRAM. Constraint matrix for SOCP (Eq. 5) also stored in QRAM. Block encoding cost (zeta, 2 log n); update O(log^2 n) per entry.
problem_formulation.constraints: Equality: mu^T x=R and Ax=b; inequality: x>=0 plus SOCP conic constraint t0 >= ||M x||.

dataset_specification.description: Main experiment: 50 companies, 100 days. Scaling study: 100 random companies, random t in [10, 500] days per instance, precision eps=0.1.

hardware.device_name: classical simulation of noisy quantum IPM (Gaussian tomography-precision noise)

noise_model.noise_type: Gaussian noise with magnitude equal to tomography precision (simulating quantum-state tomography error in the inner linear-system solve)
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Norm estimation + tomography (Kerenidis-Prakash, Theorem 6.4); no separate QEC or mitigation layer

results.notes: Fig 5: least-squares power-law fit of observed complexity vs n (eps=0.1). 95% CI [2.184, 2.589]. Implies quantum algorithm scales as O(n^2.387) vs classical O(n^3.5) in practice -> nearly O(n) speedup.
Fig 4: 1/delta^2 grows roughly linearly with n; 95% CI [0.965, 1.136].
Section 7: zeta < 5 across all instances; zeta >= 1 always, deemed not a bottleneck.
Fig 3a/3b: condition number kappa of the Newton matrix does not grow with problem size; large only in small number of instances.
Fig 1: quantum sigma = 1 - alpha/sqrt(r) with alpha close to the classical constant 0.1; asymptotically matching iteration count O(sqrt(r) log(n/eps)).

classical_baselines.method_name: Classical short-step IPM for SOCP / QP (practical omega approx 3)
classical_baselines.notes: Complexity O(sqrt(r) n^omega log(1/eps)) with omega theoretical ~2.373 but practical ~3, giving ~n^3.5 in practice.

classical_baselines.method_name: Lloyd-Rebentrost 2018 quantum algorithm (unconstrained portfolio optimization via HHL)
classical_baselines.notes: Prior quantum approach limited to unconstrained mean-variance; does not handle positivity/budget constraints addressed here.

speedup_claims.notes: Observed O(n^2.387) vs classical practical O(n^3.5). Theoretical: O~(n * sqrt(r) * kappa * zeta / delta^2 * log(1/eps)) vs O~(sqrt(r) * n^omega * log(1/eps)).

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O~(n * sqrt(r) * kappa * zeta / delta^2 * log(1/eps)); observed empirical O(n^2.387).
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O~(sqrt(r) * n^omega * log(1/eps)) ~ O(n^3.5) with practical matrix-inversion cost.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: QRAM and fault-tolerant quantum linear-algebra primitives (block-encoded linear system solvers, tomography); conditional on kappa, zeta, 1/delta^2 being well-behaved as empirically observed.

notes: Scaling exponents and CIs from Section 7 (experimental results). Theoretical complexity from Theorem 5.1/5.2. Dataset: cvxportfolio S&P-500 (Boyd et al.). Quantum algorithm is a simulated noisy IPM; no physical QPU used.
